title: We never knew you worshipped us, the idols say.
subtitle: Allah as witness to the denial
then: Continuing the scene of the Day, Ibn Kathir explains the false partners' reply: {trap}we never called you to worship us, never ordered it, never accepted it.{/trap} They call on {idea}Allah as sufficient witness{/idea} between them and those who worshipped them.
now: You refresh the celebrity's page, defend them in comment threads, model your life on theirs. {trap}They have no idea you exist.{/trap} Devotion poured into something that cannot know you is devotion lost.
old: The things I devote myself to know and value me back.
new: Only Allah truly knows my devotion. Everything else is unaware of me.
try: Count the hours you gave today to something that does not know you. Give ten minutes to Allah instead.

title: Every soul faces exactly what it sent ahead.
subtitle: The return to the true Master
then: Ibn Kathir says on that Day {idea}every soul shall know all it had sent forth, good and evil.{/idea} He cites: read your book, you are enough as a reckoner against yourself. And {trap}everything they invented to worship besides Allah simply disappears.{/trap}
now: Your screen time report arrives on Sunday. Every hour accounted for, no excuses attached. {idea}Imagine that report for every deed.{/idea} The good news: you are still writing it.
old: Most of what I do just disappears.
new: Everything I do is sent ahead, and I will meet it again.
try: Tonight, look back at your day and name one deed you would like to meet again.

title: Who feeds you, gives you sight, and runs everything?
subtitle: Questions whose answer they already knew
then: The Makkans admitted Allah was Creator and Provider. Ibn Kathir explains this {idea}admission was itself the evidence against them{/idea}: if He alone provides, controls sight and hearing, and governs everything, {trap}why worship anything else?{/trap}
now: Your eyes reading this. Your ears hearing the kettle. The salary that landed this month. {idea}You know who gave them.{/idea} The question is whether your day looks like you know.
old: I believe Allah gives me everything. That is enough.
new: Knowing He gives me everything should change how I live, not just what I say.
try: Close your eyes for ten seconds, then open them and thank Allah for your sight.

title: After the truth, what is left except error?
subtitle: There is no middle ground beyond the truth
then: Having made them admit Allah does all of this, the verse concludes: {idea}that is Allah, your Lord in truth.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says anything worshipped besides Him {trap}is false.{/trap} So how can you turn away from Him knowing He made and governs everything?
now: You know which choice is right. You still look for a version where you can keep both. {trap}The comfortable maybe.{/trap} The verse says once the truth is clear, what is left over is not a middle path.
old: I can stay undecided and that is neutral.
new: Once I know the truth, turning from it is not neutral, it is drifting into error.
try: Pick one thing you know is right and keep sitting on the fence about. Choose today.

title: Persistent defiance closes the door to belief.
subtitle: When the word of Allah comes true on the rebellious
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the idolators {trap}knew Allah was Creator and Sustainer, yet persisted{/trap} in worshipping others. Because they kept at it, {trap}the Word of Allah proved true against them.{/trap} The issue was not one slip but stubborn persistence.
now: The first time you ignore your conscience, it nags. The tenth time, it whispers. The hundredth, it is quiet. {idea}Persistence shapes the heart.{/idea} The good news: turning back also becomes easier each time.
old: I can keep ignoring this, and turn around whenever I like.
new: Each time I persist against what I know, turning back gets harder.
try: Act on one quiet nudge of conscience today before it fades.

title: Can any of your partners start creation and repeat it?
subtitle: Only Allah begins and returns creation
then: Ibn Kathir asks with the verse: {idea}who started the heavens and earth, placed the stars, and can repeat it all?{/idea} Only Allah, alone. {trap}So how are you deluded away from the truth?{/trap}
now: You give your phone the first look in the morning and the last at night. It cannot make a single cell. {idea}The One who made you, and will remake you,{/idea} often gets what is left.
old: I give my attention to what feels most useful.
new: The One who creates and recreates deserves my first attention.
try: Tomorrow morning, say a short dhikr before you touch your phone.

title: Follow the guide, not one who needs guiding.
subtitle: Who is worthy to be followed
then: Ibn Kathir asks: will a servant {idea}follow the One who guides to the truth so he may see after blindness{/idea}, or one who {trap}leads only to blindness{/trap}? He recalls Ibrahim asking his father why he worshipped what cannot hear or see.
now: The influencer who has no idea where their own life is going is telling you how to live yours. {trap}A guide who needs a guide.{/trap} Before you follow anyone, ask where they are heading.
new: I follow the One who actually knows the way.
try: Unfollow one account today that pulls you away from Allah.

title: Guesswork is no match for the truth.
subtitle: Following assumption instead of evidence
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}did not follow their religion out of evidence and proof, but mere conjecture and imagination.{/trap} And {idea}conjecture is no substitute for the truth.{/idea} Allah knows what they do.
now: "I heard that..." "Someone said..." You form a strong opinion about a person, a ruling, a news story, from a screenshot. {trap}Assumption feels like knowledge until the facts arrive.{/trap}
old: My strong feeling about it is good enough.
new: A guess, however confident, cannot stand against the truth.
try: Before stating one strong opinion today, ask yourself: how do I actually know this?

title: No one but Allah could have produced this Quran.
subtitle: It confirms what came before and explains it
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the eloquence, clarity, and precision of the Quran cannot be but from Allah.{/idea} The Arabs prized poetry above all arts, yet {reward}those who believed did so because of what they felt in its beauty and benefit.{/reward}
now: You hear a recitation in a car park and it stops you mid-step. You do not know every word, but something in it lands. {idea}That feeling has a source.{/idea} Many have believed because of it.
old: The Quran is a religious text like any other.
new: Its words carry a mark no human speech carries.
try: Listen to one short surah today with full attention, eyes closed.

title: He made it up? Then bring one surah like it.
subtitle: The open challenge to produce a single chapter
then: Ibn Kathir explains the challenge came in stages: {idea}first the whole Quran, then ten surahs, then just one.{/idea} The people of Makkah were masters of poetry. {trap}Still, none could answer it.{/trap}
now: Someone online says the Quran is just borrowed ideas. You feel a flicker of doubt. {idea}The challenge is still open, centuries later.{/idea} Doubt can be the start of looking closer, not the end.
old: When someone attacks the Quran, I feel defenceless.
new: The Quran has stood its own challenge for centuries. I can study it calmly.
try: Read the meaning of one short surah today, slowly, line by line.

title: They rejected what they never understood.
subtitle: Denying before knowing
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}did not believe in the Quran and had not yet grasped or comprehended it.{/trap} They belied it out of ignorance, just as past nations did. {idea}Look at how those nations ended.{/idea}
now: You dismiss a lecture after the first minute. You reject an idea because of who said it, not what it says. {trap}Rejecting before understanding{/trap} feels like confidence. It is often just not listening.
old: I already know enough to judge it.
new: Before I reject something, I owe it real understanding.
try: Read one thing you disagree with today all the way to the end before forming a view.

title: Some will believe, some will not. Allah knows who.
subtitle: Leaving outcomes to the One who knows
then: Ibn Kathir says among those the Prophet ﷺ was sent to, {reward}some would believe, follow, and benefit{/reward}, and {trap}some would die refusing.{/trap} Allah knows best who deserves guidance.
now: You share something beneficial in the family group chat. One cousin replies with a heart, another with an eye-roll emoji. {idea}Your job was to share it kindly.{/idea} What happens next is not in your hands.
old: If they do not accept it, I failed.
new: I convey with kindness. Who accepts is known to Allah.
try: Share one beneficial thing with someone today, and let go of how they react.

title: My deeds are mine, and yours are yours.
subtitle: A calm reply to being rejected
then: When the idolators rejected him, the Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {idea}for me are my deeds and for you are yours.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to Surah Al-Kafirun and to Ibrahim telling his people {idea}we are free of what you worship.{/idea}
now: The argument in the comments has gone forty replies deep. You keep typing. {idea}You can stop.{/idea} Say what is true once, then step away. Your record is your own, and so is theirs.
old: If they reject me, I have to keep arguing until I win.
new: I can be clear, then let each of us carry our own deeds.
try: Leave one argument today, online or offline, with a calm last sentence.

title: They hear your words, but can you make the deaf hear?
subtitle: Listening is not the same as hearing
then: Ibn Kathir says some listened to the Prophet ﷺ, his beautiful speech and the Quran. {idea}But guiding people to the truth was not up to him or them.{/idea} {trap}You cannot make the deaf hear{/trap}, except if Allah wills.
now: You have explained it to your brother five times, each time better. He nods and changes nothing. {idea}It is not your eloquence that opens hearts.{/idea} Keep being kind, and make dua for him.
old: If I find the perfect words, they will change.
new: I do my part. Opening hearts belongs to Allah.
try: Make one dua today for someone you have been trying to convince.
